Le Global Africa Tech 2026, tenu du 28 a: The Global Africa Tech 2026, held from March 28 to 30, 2026, at the Abdelatif Rahal International Conference Center in Algiers, brought together more than 5,000 participants from 45 African countries, including 50 ministers, to discuss the continent's digital sovereignty. Organized under the high patronage of President Abdelmadjid Tebboune by the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, this unprecedented pan-African event focused on four pillars: Land (terrestrial networks and fiber optics), Air (space communications), Sea (submarine cables), and Space, under the slogan "All networks, a single convergence".
Les débats ont porté sur la sécurisation: Debates focused on securing submarine cables, which carry 95% of international data traffic, and the need to diversify connectivity routes to strengthen African autonomy. Discussions also covered data centers, cross-border networks, and satellite programs under the auspices of the African Space Agency, aiming for a unified vision by 2030. The summit resulted in the Algiers Declaration on Telecommunications Sovereignty and Integrated Connectivity 2026-2030.
Importance StratégiqueLe Premier ministr: Strategic ImportanceThe Prime Minister, instructed by President Tebboune, chaired the opening, highlighting the summit's role as a platform to harmonize public policies, investments, and digital innovations. This event positions Algeria as a leader in digital infrastructure diplomacy, fostering inter-African cooperation in the face of connectivity challenges. The proceedings emphasized digital transformation for education, health, and continental security.
